name: Hub Pro

verification.note: Seen on a device running modem firmware 0x9D: a Hub Pro whose address Insteon's staging get-info page listed with category 0x03 and subcategory 0x3A answered a Get Insteon Engine Version request (cmd1 0x0D) from a Hub 2245's modem with i2CS. It wasn't linked to that modem, and it gave no category, subcategory, firmware or product key in answer to the ID Request. HouseLinc Device Definitions (version 2.9.87) lists this Hub Pro only for subcategories 0x18, 0x2C and 0x2D, so no document gives the engine for 0x3A.

steps.text: Connect the Hub to the internet and to a power outlet using the cables provided. Avoid switched outlets and filtered power strips.
On an iPhone or iPod touch with iCloud Keychain turned on, download Insteon+ from the App Store, allow it access to your HomeKit accessory data, and create an account or sign in.
Navigate to your home, tap the Add button in the upper right corner and tap Add a Device.
Tap Hub Pro at the bottom of the screen. It may take several minutes after connecting the Hub to power before it appears.
Enter the 8-digit Accessory Setup Code found on the bottom of the Hub, then give the Hub a name and pick an icon.

notes: Insteon+ requires a properly configured iCloud Keychain; if it is off or pending, the app cannot complete basic tasks like adding a device.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button.
While holding the SET button, reconnect the Hub to power.
Continue holding the SET button until the Hub stops beeping.

steps.expect: Hub double-beeps again; it has been restored to factory settings

notes: A factory reset also resets the HomeKit pairing, so the Hub can be added to a different HomeKit house.
Sold as a HomeKit bridge, which current versions of HomeKit no longer support.

Seen on an early unit whose only label was a HomeKit ID sticker marked stage, running firmware s:1.0.8.9-stage|c:5.0.6 with modem firmware 0x9D and the app version HubPro-V02, as Insteon's staging get-info page listed it, along with the device category 0x03 and subcategory 0x3A: nothing answered on ports 25105, 25106 or 9761, and ports 22, 80, 443 and 8020 accepted connections. Port 22 announced OpenSSH_6.6.1p1 Ubuntu-2ubuntu2 on connect. Port 8020 answered GET / with a 404 File Not Found. Whether units that shipped serve the Hub interface on port 25105 as the other Hubs do hasn't been verified.

Seen on the same unit: port 80 answered POST /settings with no body by returning the error Invalid JSON content. With a JSON object, empty or naming the command, it returned only {"command": "settings"} and no settings. GET / without credentials returned 401 with no WWW-Authenticate header. GET /settings without credentials returned 200 with JSON holding the network settings (address, dns, gateway, mask, mode and port), the time, and the versions of the config (5.0.6) and the server (1.0.8.9-stage), each with empty rollback and update fields. GET /buffstatus.xml and GET /3?0260=I=3 returned 404 on ports 80 and 8020.

Seen on the same unit: port 443 served TLS 1.2 with a 2048-bit key and a certificate issued to Insteon that was valid from 2013-05-06 to 2014-05-06, so it had expired. The certificate was self-signed, so a client that checks certificates refused it. With checking off, port 443 answered POST /settings with a JSON object and GET / without credentials the same way port 80 did.
Sold as the 2243-222 in the US, 2243-422 in Europe, 2243-442 in the UK and 2243-522 in Australia and New Zealand.
